You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

name: arc-block-compression
description: Use when ARC grids may compress by repeated rectangular blocks. Infer block-to-cell mapping from demos and verify before submitting.
---

# ARC block compression

Use when a demo transforms a large tiled input into a smaller grid, especially when dimensions suggest uniform blocks (for example 24×24 to 8×8 implies 3×3 patches).

## Procedure
1. Calculate the scale factor from input/output dimensions; verify both row and column factors agree.
2. Partition the input into non-overlapping blocks of that size, aligned at the top-left. A block corresponds to the output cell at the same block-row/block-column index.
3. Compare several blocks—including empty-looking and mixed-color blocks—to the demo output. Identify neutral/background colors and whether the output depends on the dominant remaining color, a specific marker, presence, count, or some other statistic.
4. Verify the proposed mapping for every output cell in all available demonstrations. Do not extrapolate from one region or assume that the largest color count is always decisive; establish neutral colors and tie/no-marker behavior explicitly.
5. Apply to the test grid and preserve output dimensions. Double-check transcription and recompute suspicious blocks; a single missed cell can change the winning color.

## Caution
This is a hypothesis class, not a universal rule. Compression may use a different block size, alignment, statistic, or output convention. Demo requests have a cost, so request another only when plausible mappings disagree on the test and a demonstration could discriminate them.",
